title: Manufacturing
summary: Discrete and general manufacturers use PI System for energy management systems, OEE and event-based analysis of batches, downtime and excursions. Standard data models across plants make benchmarking and best-practice sharing possible.
hierarchy:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  E[Enterprise] --> S[Site]
  S --> A[Area]
  A --> WC[Work Centre or Production Line]
  WC --> WU[Work Unit or Machine]
  A --> EM[Energy Meter]
```

tags.name: Fuel Gas Flow
tags.description: Fuel gas flow on a boiler; its average is captured on excursion event frames.

tags.name: Energy
tags.description: Energy consumption per area for an energy management system.

tags.name: Machine State
tags.description: Running or stopped state used for downtime events.

templates.name: Area energy meter
templates.description: Energy meter per area feeding a centralised energy monitoring system (EnMS). Illustrative.

calculations.name: Event average
calculations.expression: Fuel Gas Flow.Avg over the event frame
calculations.description: OSIsoft example: an excursion event on asset Boiler-352 carries summary attributes such as Fuel Gas Flow.Avg.

eventFrames.name: Excursion
eventFrames.trigger: A value is outside its limits, e.g. type "High Violation" on Boiler-352 lasting 12 min 24 sec

kpis.name: OEE
kpis.definition: Overall Equipment Effectiveness, the day-to-day KPI at dsm-firmenich.

kpis.name: Energy consumption
kpis.definition: Energy used per site; Michelin reported reductions of 3% to 16%.

kpis.name: OEE breakdown losses
kpis.definition: OEE losses caused by breakdowns; Syensqo reported a 50% reduction.

pitfalls: Large differences in plant monitoring capability and no standard data model block benchmarking (Toyota).
Henkel's OEE/energy story and P&G's 90-plant standardisation use AVEVA MES/System Platform, not PI; do not cite them as PI cases.
verifyNote: The ISA-95 AF hierarchy and the area energy meter template are inferred. Automotive and semiconductor PI deployments beyond Toyota and IBM were not read.
